priorStories.headline: Hurricane Isaias makes landfall near Destin
priorStories.body:
Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin around 8:30 p.m. CDT with maximum sustained winds of 105 mph, the National Hurricane Center said. It had reached Category 3 strength earlier Friday.

By 10 p.m., Isaias was inland and its maximum winds had fallen to an estimated 90 mph. Damaging winds, storm surge and flash flooding remained hazards.

priorStories.headline: Magnitude 7.6 earthquake strikes Panama
priorStories.body:
A magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck central Panama at 17:56 UTC, according to the U.S. Geological Survey. The Associated Press reported two powerful earthquakes and numerous aftershocks.

Some buildings near the epicenter partially collapsed, and evacuations occurred across the country. Officials reported several injuries but no immediate deaths.

priorStories.headline: Simon becomes Category 3 hurricane off Mexico
priorStories.body:
Hurricane Simon strengthened to Category 3 with maximum sustained winds of 120 mph by 9 p.m. CST. Its center was about 155 miles south of Manzanillo.

A hurricane warning remained in effect along Mexico’s coast from Punta San Telmo to Punta Mita.

priorStories.headline: U.S. eases sanctions for Russian diesel
priorStories.body:
The Treasury Department issued a temporary license easing sanctions on Russian diesel loaded onto tankers beginning Friday.

President Donald Trump said he had reached an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin for Russia to supply diesel to the United States and global markets. Trump said the initial shipment would exceed 300,000 tons.

candidates.summary: Isaias became a post-tropical cyclone over southern Alabama at 1 a.m. CDT, with maximum sustained winds of 65 mph. More than 726,000 electricity customers in Florida and Alabama were without power early Saturday, while flooded roads, downed trees and power lines were reported across the region.
candidates.title: Isaias weakens as widespread outages hit Florida and Alabama

candidates.summary: The U.S. Geological Survey recorded a magnitude 6.0 earthquake at 04:14 UTC about 7 kilometers north of La Tronosa, Panama, at a depth of 10 kilometers. It followed the previous day’s two powerful earthquakes and continuing aftershock sequence.
candidates.title: Magnitude 6.0 aftershock strikes Panama

candidates.summary: By 10 a.m. CDT, Isaias was a post-tropical cyclone near Birmingham, Alabama, with maximum sustained winds of 35 mph. Flood watches covered parts of the Southeast and southern Appalachians, and high-wind warnings covered northeastern Alabama, northern Georgia and the southern Appalachians. The Associated Press reported more than 911,000 customers without power across Florida, Alabama and Georgia early Saturday.
candidates.title: Isaias weakens further as flood risk and widespread outages persist

candidates.summary: Police detained more than 2,000 protesters and leaders of India’s youth-led “Cockroach” movement as authorities restricted access, transport and mobile internet in parts of New Delhi. The planned demonstration demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a disputed voter-list revision. The Election Commission and government deny allegations that the revision manipulates voter rolls.
candidates.title: Thousands detained as authorities disrupt New Delhi election protest

candidates.summary: Two Israeli strikes killed at least five Palestinians in Gaza City, according to local health officials. Four people were reported killed near Panda Mall and one in the Tuffah neighborhood. The Israeli military said the strikes targeted militants but did not provide further details.
candidates.title: Israeli strikes kill five people in Gaza City

candidates.summary: Germany said it would maintain sanctions against Russia and work with European partners on further measures despite the United States temporarily easing restrictions on Russian diesel. Government spokesperson Stefan Kornelius said Germany’s support for Ukraine remained unchanged.
candidates.title: Germany says Russian sanctions will remain despite U.S. diesel decision

candidates.summary: Lawyer Miriam González Durántez launched Democracy21, a new centrist Spanish political party, to contest the November 29 snap general election in Madrid and Barcelona. She said the party would seek to bridge Spain’s ideological divide and depoliticize public institutions.
candidates.title: Miriam González Durántez launches Spanish centrist party

candidates.summary: A Saturday attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh killed 12 people and wounded dozens, Reuters reported, citing three people familiar with the matter; Saudi authorities had not issued an official casualty toll. Airport operations were temporarily suspended and flights were diverted. The Associated Press reported that a missile struck the domestic-terminal complex and that many people were wounded.
candidates.title: Riyadh airport attack reportedly kills 12 people

candidates.summary: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas issued a decree canceling legislative elections scheduled for November 28, 2026, and setting simultaneous presidential and legislative elections for September 11, 2027. The Palestinian presidency cited security, logistical and on-the-ground obstacles.
candidates.title: Abbas postpones Palestinian elections until September 2027

candidates.summary: Hurricane Simon strengthened to Category 4 off Mexico’s Pacific coast. The National Hurricane Center estimated maximum sustained winds of 145 mph at 09:00 UTC; Reuters reported winds had subsequently reached 150 mph as Simon moved north toward west-central Mexico. Hurricane warnings covered parts of the coast, including the Manzanillo area and Islas Marías.
candidates.title: Simon strengthens to Category 4 off Mexico

candidates.summary: Three people were injured in a stabbing at a private post-secondary school in Warsaw’s Praga district, according to Reuters. It was the third youth stabbing attack reported in Poland within four days.
candidates.title: Three injured in Warsaw school stabbing

candidates.summary: Christa Pike was discharged from a hospital and returned to Tennessee’s Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center after surviving the state’s attempted lethal-injection execution. Her attorneys said she would continue receiving medical care in prison.
candidates.title: Christa Pike returns to prison after surviving execution attempt

candidates.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio pledged cooperation with Japanese authorities investigating allegations that a U.S. Marine murdered a woman in Okinawa. The case prompted protests and led the U.S. military to impose a curfew and mandatory standards-and-discipline training.
candidates.title: U.S. pledges cooperation in Okinawa murder investigation
